units.text: This note was written for the billing team's architecture review and replaces the earlier draft shared in chat.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs

units.text: The billing service runs about 40,000 background jobs a day: rendering invoice PDFs, sending receipt emails and retrying failed webhooks.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Context

units.text: Today they run in an in-process worker pool, so a deploy or a crash loses any job that was queued but not yet started.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Context

units.text: Last quarter that lost 37 invoice emails that customers had to request again.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Context

units.text: Peak load is 600 jobs per minute, during the month-end billing run.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Context

units.text: **Option A: managed cloud queue.** A queue service run by our cloud provider.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: We send messages to it and workers poll for them; the provider handles storage, scaling and redelivery.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: **Option B: self-hosted broker.** A message broker cluster of three virtual machines that we install, patch and monitor ourselves.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: **Option C: database job table.** A `jobs` table in the existing billing Postgres database.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: Workers claim rows with `SELECT ...
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and mark them done.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Options

units.text: Option | Monthly infrastructure | Monthly team effort | Notes
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: Managed cloud queue | $310 | about 2 hours | Priced per million requests; grows with volume
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: Self-hosted broker | $540 | about 12 hours | Three VMs plus upgrades and on-call
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: Database job table | $0 extra | about 4 hours | Uses spare capacity on the existing primary
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: The managed queue's figure assumes current volume.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: At three times today's volume it would be roughly $900 a month, while the broker's cost would stay flat until the cluster needs a fourth machine.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Costs

units.text: Two criteria are must-haves; an option that fails either is out regardless of its score:
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: No job is lost when a worker crashes or the service is deployed.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: The queue absorbs 1,800 jobs per minute (three times today's peak) without manual intervention.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: The remaining criteria are weighted for scoring:
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: Operational effort: 40%
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: Monthly cost: 30%
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: Developer experience, including local testing: 20%
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: Portability away from our cloud provider: 10%
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Selection criteria

units.text: Option A needs almost no operational work, and failed messages move to a dead-letter queue automatically.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: The catch is that the service delivers each message at least once, so every job handler must be made idempotent before we switch; today only the email handler is.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: It also ties us to one provider's API, and local development needs an emulator that does not support dead-lettering.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: Option B gives us priority queues and delayed delivery, which would let month-end invoices jump ahead of webhook retries.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: No one on the team has run this broker in production, so the 12 hours a month is an estimate, not a measurement.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: Upgrades need a maintenance window.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: Option C writes a job in the same transaction as the billing change that causes it, so a job can never be lost between the commit and the enqueue.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: That guarantee only covers jobs created inside the billing database transaction; jobs enqueued by the reporting service, which has its own database, would not get it.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: Polling also adds read load to the primary database, which is the main risk at month-end.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Benefits and trade-offs

units.text: We load-tested Option C on a staging copy of the database with synthetic jobs.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: At 2,000 jobs per minute, primary CPU reached 85% and p95 latency rose to 240 ms.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: We did not test 1,800 jobs per minute, and the staging copy is about a quarter of production size, so these results may not carry over.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: We have not load-tested Options A or B.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: The provider documents throughput far above our peak for Option A, but that is the provider's figure, not ours.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Evidence

units.text: This note does not recommend an option.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: The decision is deferred until Option C has been measured at 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Until then, each option carries an open requirement:
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Option A: every job handler made idempotent.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Option B: a named owner for broker on-call and upgrades.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Option C: a passing load test at 1,800 jobs per minute.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Priya will bring the load-test result to the next architecture review.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status

units.text: Thanks to everyone who commented on the first draft.
units.topic: Choosing a queue for background jobs › Decision status
